::: course-content
[Workshop]{.course-badge}

## Follow-Up Workshop: Single Cell Data Analysis

<p class="lead">

Join the team at the Hub for Applied Bioinformatics @ King's College London for this workshop which will equip researchers with the practical R skills needed to independently process, visualise, and critically analyse single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets.

</p>

### About the Workshop

Single-cell transcriptomics is a powerful tool to study the heterogeneity of the cellular transcriptome at single-cell levels.

Designed as the practical Part 2 companion to the King’s Health Partners [Next-Generation Sequencing online module](https://learninghub.kingshealthpartners.org/course/ngs-single-cell-rna-sequencing-analysis), this in-person course aims to equip participants with essential skills to process RNA-sequencing reads from single-cell transcriptomics experiment and to perform downstream analyses of the single-cell gene expression data. 

This course is designed for participants with some experience in R programming and running command-line programs. Published single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets will be used to perform quality control, data normalisation, cell clustering, differential expression and trajectory analyses. 

We will use the 
Objects produced from the online workshop will be used, along with other single-cell datasets, to expand on the important aspects of single-cell analysis, discuss decision-making steps along the analysis pipeline, visualise the data differently, and perform additional analysis. Due to the focused three-hour timeframe, practical exercises will utilise fast, R-based tools, supplemented by case study discussions where relevant.

### What you will learn

By the end of this session, you will be able to independently conduct and critically evaluate scRNA-seq data analyses, including:

- Performing quality control and data normalisation on single-cell gene expression data.
- Executing cell clustering and exploring alternative ways to visualise single-cell datasets.
- Conducting differential expression and trajectory analyses.
- Navigating critical decision-making steps throughout an R-based single-cell analysis pipeline.

### Audience

This course is designed for researchers and practitioners looking to advance their practical capabilities in single-cell transcriptomics who have already completed the prerequisite online Innovations Scholar Workshop.

### Prerequisites

To attend this in-person session, participants must have prior experience in R programming and running command-line programs. In addition, you must complete the following requirements prior to arrival:

- Completion of the associated online module: [**NGS: Single-cell RNA-sequencing Analysis**](https://learninghub.kingshealthpartners.org/course/ngs-single-cell-rna-sequencing-analysis). It will take approximately 7 hours to complete the online materials. 
- Software Setup: Have RStudio installed along with all R libraries used during the online session.
- Data Files: Bring the .RDS object obtained from the online workshop.

For further information about the session, visit the [official workshop page](https://hab.sites.er.kcl.ac.uk/event/single-cell-data-analysis/) or email hab@kcl.ac.uk

 
### Location 

The workshop will take place at the Hub for Applied Bioinformatics in the Hodgkins Building, Guy’s Campus.

The HAB space is located on the ground floor of the Hodgkin building at the Guy’s campus (room G60).

**Venue Details** Hodgkins Building, Guy’s Campus, Room G60, Newcomen St, London, SE1 1UL
